name: Summarize a text
description: Pulls out the key points of a long text, then writes a short summary.
instructions: Be faithful to the text. Do not add facts that are not in it. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Key points
steps.prompt: List the 5 to 8 most important points of the text I gave, one short line each. Facts, names, numbers and decisions first. Do not write the summary yet.

steps.title: Write the summary
steps.prompt: Using only the key points above, write a clear summary of 3 to 5 sentences. Start with the main idea. Do not add anything new.

name: Proofread and rewrite
description: Finds the problems in a text, then rewrites it cleanly.
instructions: Keep the author's meaning and voice. Fix, do not invent. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Find problems
steps.prompt: Read my text and list its problems: spelling, grammar, unclear or too long sentences, repetitions. One short line per problem, quoting the words. Do not rewrite yet.

steps.title: Rewrite
steps.prompt: Rewrite my original text fixing every problem listed above. Keep the meaning and the length close to the original. Give only the corrected text.

steps.title: Changes
steps.prompt: In 3 to 5 short bullet points, say what you changed and why.

name: Translate with check
description: Translates a text, checks it against the original, then gives the final version.
instructions: Keep the tone, names and numbers. If the target language is not given, ask nothing and translate to English. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Translate
steps.prompt: Translate my text into the language I asked for. Give only the translation.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Compare the translation above with the original text. List any meaning that is missing, added or wrong, and any unnatural phrase. If everything is correct, say OK.

steps.title: Final version
steps.prompt: Give the final translation with the corrections from the check applied. Give only the text.

name: Explain simply
description: Explains a topic from the basics, with an example and an analogy.
instructions: Use short sentences and everyday words. Define any technical word the first time. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.prompt: Explain the topic I asked about in 2 or 3 very simple sentences, as to a 10-year-old. No jargon.

steps.title: Example
steps.prompt: Give one concrete everyday example and one analogy that make the explanation above easier to picture.

steps.title: Step by step
steps.prompt: Now explain it again in 4 to 6 numbered steps, a little more precisely, building on the answers above. End with one question to check understanding.

name: Study notes and quiz
description: Turns a text or topic into short study notes, then practice questions.
instructions: Be accurate and short. Use only the given text, or common knowledge if only a topic is given. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Study notes
steps.prompt: Write study notes on my text or topic: 6 to 10 short bullet points with the key facts, terms and definitions.

steps.title: Questions
steps.prompt: From the notes above, write 6 questions of mixed difficulty, numbered. Do not give the answers yet.

steps.title: Answers
steps.prompt: Give the short answer to each question above, with the same numbers.

name: Email writer
description: Writes a clear email from your facts, then polishes the tone.
instructions: Be polite, clear and brief. Never invent names, dates or promises. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Facts
steps.prompt: From my request, list in short bullets: who it is for, the goal, the key facts, and what I expect as a reply. If something is missing, write it as [to fill].

steps.title: Draft
steps.prompt: Write the email from those facts: a subject line, a greeting, a short body of 2 to 3 short paragraphs and a closing.

steps.title: Polish
steps.prompt: Improve the draft above: shorter sentences, a polite and natural tone, one clear request. Give only the final email, with the subject.

name: Meeting notes to actions
description: Turns raw meeting notes into decisions and a list of actions.
instructions: Use only what is in the notes. If an owner or a date is not stated, write 'unassigned' or 'no date'. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Decisions
steps.prompt: From the meeting notes I gave, list the decisions that were made and the open questions, as short bullets.

steps.title: Actions
steps.prompt: List every action to do: task, owner, due date. One line each, in the form: Task - Owner - Date.

steps.title: Summary
steps.prompt: Write a meeting summary of at most 5 lines: topic, decisions, next actions. Use the lists above.

name: Brainstorm ideas
description: Generates many ideas, picks the best three and develops them.
instructions: Be concrete and varied. Avoid vague ideas. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Many ideas
steps.prompt: List 10 different ideas for my request, one short line each. Mix safe and original ones.

steps.title: Pick the best
steps.prompt: From the ideas above choose the 3 best for my goal. For each, give one line saying why it is good.

steps.title: Expand
steps.prompt: Develop each of the 3 chosen ideas: what it is, the first 3 steps to start, and one risk to watch.

name: Decision helper
description: Lists pros and cons of a choice, weighs them and recommends an option.
instructions: Be balanced and practical. Base the advice on my situation. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Options
steps.prompt: Name the options in my question (at least two) and the criteria that matter, in short bullets.

steps.title: Pros and cons
steps.prompt: For each option, list 3 pros and 3 cons, one short line each, using the criteria above.

steps.title: Recommendation
steps.prompt: Weigh the pros and cons above and recommend one option in 3 to 4 sentences. Say what would change your mind.

name: Project plan
description: Splits a project into tasks, orders them and gives a simple schedule.
instructions: Tasks must be small and actionable, starting with a verb. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Goal and scope
steps.prompt: State the project goal in one sentence and list what is in and out of scope, in short bullets.

steps.title: Tasks
steps.prompt: Break the project into 8 to 12 small tasks, numbered, each starting with a verb.

steps.title: Order and schedule
steps.prompt: Put the tasks above in a sensible order, group them in 3 phases, and give a rough time estimate for each phase.

name: Recipe and meal planner
description: Suggests meals from your constraints, then writes the recipe and shopping list.
instructions: Keep recipes simple and realistic. Respect diets and allergies. Quantities for the number of people given. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Constraints
steps.prompt: List my constraints in short bullets: people, diet, allergies, time, ingredients at hand. Then suggest 3 meal ideas that fit.

steps.title: Recipe
steps.prompt: Take the first meal above and write its recipe: ingredients with quantities, then 5 to 8 short numbered steps.

steps.title: Shopping list
steps.prompt: Write the shopping list for that recipe, grouped by type (vegetables, dairy, pantry...). Leave out what I said I already have.

name: Code explainer
description: Reads code, explains what it does, then suggests improvements.
instructions: Refer to the code's own names. Keep explanations short. Plain text, code in code fences only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Read
steps.prompt: State in 2 sentences what the code I gave does, then list its main parts (functions, inputs, outputs).

steps.title: Explain
steps.prompt: Explain the code above step by step in plain words, following its order. Keep it to 6 short bullets at most.

steps.title: Improve
steps.prompt: Suggest up to 4 improvements (clarity, safety, speed, naming) based on the explanation above. Show a short code snippet only where it helps.

name: Bug finder
description: Reads code for bugs, ranks them and proposes fixes.
instructions: Only report real problems you can point to in the code. Say which line or name. Code in code fences only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Suspects
steps.prompt: Read the code and error I gave. List possible bugs, one line each, naming the line or function. Include edge cases like empty input or null.

steps.title: Most likely cause
steps.prompt: Pick the most likely cause from the list above and explain in 3 sentences why it produces the problem.

steps.title: Fix
steps.prompt: Show the corrected code for that cause in a code fence, then list in one line how to test that it is fixed.

name: Text to table
description: Extracts the data of a text into a clean markdown table.
instructions: Use only data present in the text. Use '-' for missing values. Plain text and markdown tables only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Columns
steps.prompt: Look at the text I gave and decide the best columns for a table. List them in one line, with what each column holds.

steps.title: Table
steps.prompt: Write a markdown table with those columns, one row per item in the text. Keep values short and exact.

name: Daily planner
description: Sorts your tasks by priority and builds a realistic schedule for the day.
instructions: Be realistic: include breaks and leave slack. Do not add tasks I did not mention. Plain text only. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Tasks
steps.prompt: List the tasks from my message, one per line, with an estimated duration and whether it is urgent or important.

steps.title: Priorities
steps.prompt: Sort the tasks above into: Do first, Do next, Can wait. One short reason each.

steps.title: Schedule
steps.prompt: Build an hour-by-hour schedule for my day from the priorities above, with breaks. Use the times I gave, or 9:00 to 18:00 if none.

name: Chart or diagram helper
description: Prepares the data or the flow, then draws it with a chart or mermaid block.
instructions: Never invent numbers: use only those I gave. Keep labels short. Draw only in the last step. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Understand
steps.prompt: Decide whether my request is a chart (numbers) or a diagram (steps, flow, relations). List the data points or the nodes and links, in short bullets.

steps.title: Draw
steps.prompt: Using the list above, draw it. If it is numbers, use a chart block with a title, labels and values. If it is a flow or relations, use a mermaid block. Add one sentence below it saying what it shows.

name: Website or landing page
description: Builds a one-page website from blocks (hero, features, prices, contact...) that you can edit visually.
instructions: The app builds sites from blocks and turns them into a real HTML page: the person never needs code. Never invent prices, testimonials or contact details: use placeholders the person can replace. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Brief
steps.prompt: Ask nothing. From my request, state in 4 short lines: what the site is for, who it is for, the tone, and the sections it needs (hero, features, prices, testimonials, FAQ, contact).

steps.title: Build the site
steps.prompt: Build the website now as one finished page, using the brief above. Name the file with .html. Short clear texts, one call to action.

steps.title: Improve
steps.prompt: Tell me in 3 bullet points what I can ask to change next (colours, sections, wording, animations). The Edit blocks button of the file opens the visual editor.

name: Calculator or simulator page
description: Makes a converter, simulator or calculator page (loan, BMI, tip, unit conversion) with inputs and live results.
instructions: The result is one working HTML page: inputs, a clear formula, results that update at once. State every formula you use. No invented rates or data: ask for them as inputs. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Inputs and formulas
steps.prompt: List the inputs (with a default value and a unit) and the formulas of the results, one line each.

steps.title: Build the page
steps.prompt: Build the page now from the list above, as one finished .html file, with a clean layout that works on a phone.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Take three example inputs, compute the results by hand with the formulas, and say whether the page gives the same.

name: Arcade game
description: Makes a playable game (pong, breakout, invaders, snake, platformer...) described to the game engine of the app.
instructions: Classic arcade games are described to the app's own engine (things, rules, score, lives, restart) rather than programmed from scratch. Snake, tic-tac-toe, quiz and the like start from a tested page. Keep the game simple and fun. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Game design
steps.prompt: In 6 short lines say: the goal, the controls (keys or mouse), what the player moves, what moves by itself, how you score, how you lose.

steps.title: Build the game
steps.prompt: Build the game now from the design above, as one finished .html file that starts on its own, with a score, lives and a restart.

steps.title: Play test
steps.prompt: Name the three most likely problems when this game is played (controls, collisions, difficulty) and fix any you can see.

name: Small web app or tool
description: Builds a small program on ONE page: to-do list, stopwatch, quiz game, notes, timer, tracker.
instructions: A small program is ONE .html file written whole: markup, style and script together, no library, no network. The script must find every element it uses. Save data in localStorage when it helps. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Rules
steps.prompt: List in 5 short lines what the program does, what the person can click or type, and what is saved.

steps.title: Write the program
steps.prompt: Write the whole program now as one .html file from the rules above.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Re-read the script: does every id it looks for exist in the page, and does every button do something? Fix what is wrong and give the corrected file only if you changed it.

name: Write and test code
description: Writes a program or script in the language you name, with a test case and an explanation.
instructions: Write complete, runnable code, never fragments with '...'. Use the standard library when it is enough. Put each file in its own artifact with its real file name. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Plan
steps.prompt: In 4 short lines say what the code does, its inputs and outputs, the files, and the language.

steps.title: Write
steps.prompt: Write the complete code of every file now.

steps.title: Test case
steps.prompt: Give one example run: the input and the output the code should produce, checked line by line against the code. Say if you see a bug.

steps.title: How to run
steps.prompt: Give the exact command to run it, in one or two lines.

name: Change an existing file
description: Changes the files already in the chat with small precise edits instead of rewriting everything.
instructions: Change only what was asked. Use edit blocks on the existing file; never rewrite a whole file for a small change. Keep names, style and everything that works. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: What to change
steps.prompt: List in short lines the exact changes asked, and the part of the file each one touches.

steps.title: Apply
steps.prompt: Apply the changes with edit blocks, one per change.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Re-read the result: is anything that worked now broken? Say OK or fix it.

name: PowerPoint presentation
description: Makes a presentation with a theme, a plan, short slides, charts from your own figures and speaker notes.
instructions: A presentation is a pptx file; the app lays the slides out and checks them. One idea per slide, a short title, at most 5 short bullets or one figure. Charts only from numbers the person gave: never invent numbers. Pictures only when the Pictures tool is on. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Plan
steps.prompt: Give the audience, the goal, a theme in a few words (mood and colour), and the list of slide titles in order, 6 to 12 slides.

steps.title: Build the deck
steps.prompt: Build the presentation now as a pptx file from the plan above, with speaker notes.

steps.title: Improve
steps.prompt: Say in 3 short points what to change to make it stronger (a figure, a chart, a quote) and offer to do it.

name: Word document
description: Writes a finished Word document: report, CV, letter, minutes, proposal, invoice, contract, recipe, lesson plan...
instructions: The result is a docx file made from a template; headings, short paragraphs, lists and tables. Placeholders in [brackets] for what you do not know. Never invent facts, names or amounts. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Outline
steps.prompt: Say which kind of document it is and give its section titles in order, one line each.

steps.title: Write
steps.prompt: Write the document now as a docx file from the outline above.

steps.title: Review
steps.prompt: List in 3 short points what is missing or must be filled in by the person.

when: \b(docx|(?:fichier|document|file) word|word (?:document|file|doc)|en word|in word|un word|lettre de motivation|cover letter|cv|r[ée]sum[ée]|minutes of|compte[- ]rendu|facture|invoice|contrat|contract)\b

name: Excel spreadsheet
description: Makes a spreadsheet with formulas already in place: budget, tracker, invoice, planner, gradebook, loan...
instructions: The result is an xlsx file: headers first, then rows, formulas that start with = (=B2*C2, =SUM(D2:D9), =AVG(A1:A9)). The first line is row 1, the first column is A. Totals are formulas, never typed numbers. Headers in the language of the request. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Columns
steps.prompt: List the sheets, the column headers of each, and which cells are formulas.

steps.title: Build
steps.prompt: Build the spreadsheet now as an xlsx file, with a few example rows.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Check that each formula points at the right cells and say OK or fix it.

name: Interactive chart
description: Draws a chart with sliders and formulas that the person can move, with no code.
instructions: A chart is a fenced chart block that the app draws: sliders, number fields, typeset formulas and result cards. It is not a web page. Use only numbers the person gave or clearly marked examples. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Data and parameters
steps.prompt: List the data and the parameters the person can move (with min, max, default), and the formula that links them.

steps.title: Draw
steps.prompt: Draw it now with one chart block and one short sentence.

steps.title: Reading
steps.prompt: In 2 sentences, say what the chart shows and which slider changes it most.

name: Diagram
description: Draws a flowchart, sequence, org chart, mind map, timeline, Gantt, state, class or ER diagram.
instructions: A diagram is a fenced mermaid block that the app draws; never use HTML or SVG. Short labels, no special characters in node names, at most 15 nodes. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Elements
steps.prompt: List the elements and the links between them, and say which kind of diagram fits best.

steps.title: Draw
steps.prompt: Draw it now with one mermaid block and one short sentence.

name: Quiz, flashcards or checklist
description: Makes a quiz that scores itself, flashcards to flip, or a checklist to tick, from a topic or a text.
instructions: These are fenced blocks the app runs: quiz (- wrong, + right, > explanation), cards (Question | Answer), checklist ([ ] item). Facts must come from the text given or be common knowledge. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Key facts
steps.prompt: List the 8 to 10 facts worth testing, one short line each.

steps.title: Make it
steps.prompt: Make a quiz block of 6 to 8 questions with 3 or 4 options each and an explanation for each answer.

steps.title: Cards
steps.prompt: Make a cards block of the 8 most important question and answer pairs.

name: Document with charts and tables
description: Writes a finished document (report, course, guide, fiche) with tables, figures, charts and diagrams inside.
instructions: A document is a markdown file. Where a figure, diagram, table, quiz or formula says it better than words, put the drawn block right there instead of describing it. Never draw with HTML or SVG. Answer in the language of the user's request.

steps.title: Outline
steps.prompt: Give the title and the section titles in order, with the drawn block (table, chart, mermaid, kpi, quiz) planned for each, if any.

steps.title: Write
steps.prompt: Write the whole document now as a markdown file, following the outline.

steps.title: Review
steps.prompt: Re-read it: is any section thin, and does every block have a short sentence that introduces it? Say OK or fix it.
